meta.title: Policy Window Monitor — Chile
meta.note: Pilot run. Ratings are provisional: one analyst, no double coding. A flagged window is a likely opening, not a certainty, and not an endorsement of any proposal.

topics.name: Organised crime & Rules on the Use of Force (RUF)
topics.problem: Crime is the top problem in polls (CEP 57%), with sustained attention.
topics.politics: Level 3 in W5, then 2 after the decision: the mixed-committee report was approved on 7 Oct (Cámara 111–23–5, Senate 29–15–1).
topics.policy: Eight graduated rules, from police presence to lethal force. A bill from the previous government, adopted by this one.
topics.frames: 'Security as a precondition' vs proportionality and human rights. Partially converging.
topics.changed: Sent to promulgation after three years in Congress. The debate now moves to implementation.
topics.reopen: Implementation controversy or a use-of-force incident

topics.name: Calles sin Violencia replaced by Plan FOCO
topics.problem: Level 2 in W4–W5, then 1 as attention faded. Problem broker: Carolina Tohá, who calls the programme central to reversing the rise in homicides.
topics.politics: The 2027 budget replaces Calles sin Violencia with FOCO. Barrio Prioritario is cut 43.4%; the crime-prevention undersecretariat gets +2.9%.
topics.policy: Two named alternatives compete. Undersecretary Pilar Giannini says FOCO has a stronger design and measurement; no evaluation of either is published.
topics.changed: Problem stream fell to level 1 in W6; the window stays open through politics and policy until the budget vote. The 2026 budget of the programme is reported as $26,017m (The Clinic) and $13,441m (El Mostrador).

topics.name: Migration: expulsions and detention
topics.problem: Immigration concern fell to 13% (CEP). 1,468 expulsions since March (secondary source).
topics.politics: Law dispatched on 20 Oct (Senate 37–0–1): home entry with a judicial order, re-entry ban raised from 3 to 5 years. Deputies rejected 60-day detention; the President publicly challenged them.
topics.policy: Bill adopted. A separate bill to criminalise irregular entry is pending (stage not verified).
topics.frames: Control and enforcement vs rights. Not assessed in detail.
topics.changed: Expulsions decision taken; the detention reform failed.
topics.reopen: Detention reform or irregular-entry offence revived

topics.name: Administrative sentence reductions ('caso Rabat')
topics.problem: Focusing event: 56 reductions for sexual offences against minors, plus reductions for crimes against humanity and for 115 foreign nationals convicted of drug offences. Cadem (27 Oct): 94% reject the reductions; 77% disapprove of the minister's handling.
topics.politics: Undersecretary removed. The minister announced a bill on the Ley 19.856 system and possible revocations. The opposition confirmed a three-chapter constitutional accusation (28 Oct); UDI refused to back it (4 Nov).
topics.policy: The minister advocates a named fix and has access to decision venues. No bill filed.
topics.frames: 'Illegitimate error' vs 'legal compliance'. Partially converging against the reductions.
topics.changed: The largest focusing event of the period. Presidential approval fell 7 points since the case began.

topics.name: Pension funds D and E losses
topics.problem: The Superintendent told the Cámara Labour committee (26 Oct) derivative losses were about US$10.1bn at 30 Sep, easing to about US$7bn by 20 Oct. Fund E −7.56% and Fund D −4.73% year to date. Attention fading after October's rebound.
topics.politics: Sanction process against 7 AFPs opened (20 Oct) and a committee session held. No executive bill.
topics.policy: Compensation and duration limits are mentioned, but no actor meets the entrepreneur definition.
topics.frames: Excessive portfolio duration (regulator) vs systemic failure of individual capitalisation. Not converging.
topics.changed: Problem stream weakening in W8 as funds recovered.

topics.name: Employment recovery
topics.problem: Unemployment 9.8% (Jul–Sep, INE), highest since 2021; over 1 million unemployed; women 10.5%. Manufacturing jobs −8.1%. Cadem: job-instability worry 71%.
topics.politics: The executive frames Sala Cuna as an employment measure. The SENCE training budget was rejected in the mixed committee.
topics.changed: Problem stream rose to level 3 with the 29 Oct INE release.

topics.name: Sala Cuna Universal (Boletín 14.782-13)
topics.problem: The minister frames female unemployment above 10% and the 20-female-worker threshold (Art. 203) as a hiring barrier.
topics.politics: Senate passage 8 Sep; 'discusión inmediata' urgency 21 Sep; Cámara Labour committee approved it 13–0 (20 Oct) and in particular on 4 Nov, restoring financing (0.30% employer contribution offset by lower unemployment-insurance contributions). Next: Hacienda committee.
topics.policy: Bill with a co-payment subsidy (50% for the most vulnerable 40%, 30% for the 41–60% band; regional source).
topics.frames: Employment for women vs 'negocio' (opposition criticism of the co-payment).
topics.changed: Financing restored in committee on 4 Nov; the bill moves to the Hacienda committee.

topics.name: Budget 2027 and fiscal consolidation
topics.problem: The Fiscal Council (CFA, 28 Oct) warns 2027 revenues may fall short and spending compatible with targets can grow only 0.5% a year, against 1.2% projected.
topics.politics: Budget bill submitted 30 Sep (+1.5% spending). Mood mixed: 58% see spending as inefficient, but only 19% back cutting social programmes (Criteria).
topics.policy: Government austerity path (structural balance −1.8% of GDP); restoration amendments; CFA calls for a fiscal-sustainability agreement.
topics.frames: Fiscal responsibility vs protection of social spending. Not converging.
topics.changed: Mixed committee rejected Education, primary care and SENCE (5 Nov). Floor votes 9–11 and 17–19 Nov.

topics.name: Health budget: Ricarte Soto, immunisation, primary care
topics.problem: Senator Juan Luis Castro and health unions oppose the $28,000m Ricarte Soto cut and cuts to vaccines, primary care, mental health, dental and palliative care.
topics.politics: An executive amendment supplemented Ricarte Soto. Health passed 13–11 in the mixed committee; the primary-care programme was rejected.
topics.policy: Restore Ricarte Soto (partly done); raise primary-care per-capita funding without merging programmes; protect immunisation and mental health.
topics.frames: Efficiency vs protection of guaranteed coverage. Not converging.
topics.changed: Ricarte Soto partly restored; primary care rejected in committee.

topics.name: Surgical waiting lists
topics.problem: Baseline record (Minsal, Q1 2026): 458,109 pending surgeries for 398,496 people, though the median wait fell 40 days. No new data in the period.
topics.politics: No new government action found in the period.
topics.policy: No entrepreneur found in the period.
topics.changed: Quiet in the period; next Minsal report could move it.

topics.name: Primary-care mental health
topics.problem: Raised only inside the health-budget debate.
topics.changed: Tied to the health budget vote.

topics.name: Specific excise tax on vapes
topics.problem: No Chilean problem signal in the period. (Colombian vape-tax news excluded.)
topics.politics: Hacienda's precondition, the Reconstruction law, was met with Ley 21.850 on 17 Oct, but no bill was found.
topics.policy: On 16 Jun Hacienda, with Health, said it is drafting a specific tax at rates somewhat below cigarettes; vapes now pay only 19% VAT. U. de Chile specialists back it.
topics.changed: Precondition met on 17 Oct. Trigger to watch: Hacienda filing the bill.

topics.name: Tobacco contraband and Customs
topics.problem: Revenue gap from contraband estimated by the government at about US$505m.
topics.politics: Ley 21.850 published 17 Oct; a 15.1% Customs budget cut is pending.
topics.policy: Article 10 of the Reconstruction bill: tougher penalties, mandatory criminal complaints by Customs, vehicle seizure (whether kept in the final law: to verify). Sen. Miguel Becker's bill proposes up to 20 years (status not verified).
topics.changed: Decision taken on 17 Oct; contents to verify.

topics.name: Education budget (SLEP, Yo Elijo Mi PC, Junji/Junaeb)
topics.problem: Programme feedback on SLEP teacher-hour cuts and the end of Yo Elijo Mi PC. Ximena Rubilar called on the President to explain.
topics.politics: Fell from 3 to 2 after the mixed committee rejected the whole Education budget (5 Nov). The government signalled openness to changes.
topics.policy: Restore Yo Elijo Mi PC, liceos bicentenario, learning assessment and SLEP staffing. Entrepreneur set is thin.
entrepreneurs: Opposition members of the mixed committee
topics.changed: Education budget rejected in committee on 5 Nov.

topics.name: CAE/FES student debt
topics.problem: No new problem signal in the period.
topics.politics: The previous government's bill has been in the Senate since August 2025 and stalled in January 2026. Senate Education chair Gustavo Sanhueza (UDI) has raised doubts. No urgency in the period.

topics.name: Tolls and electricity tariffs
topics.problem: Cost of living concern; no specific new indicator.
topics.politics: Announcement in W6: Autopista Central toll cut of 10–25% from January 2027 in exchange for a 20-month concession extension; lower electricity prices in 2027. Criteria: 44% oppose the concession mechanism vs 41% in favour.
topics.frames: Relief for households vs concession giveaway.

topics.name: Regional funding and Ley Cholito
topics.problem: Ley Cholito (responsible pet ownership) line cut 86% ($3,634m to $514m).
topics.politics: Minister of Finance celebrated an agreement with the regional governors on 4 Nov.
topics.changed: Agreement reached; pending the floor vote.

topics.name: Storm emergency management
topics.problem: Criteria (25 Oct): the government was the worst-evaluated institution for its storm response.

topics.name: 'Coalición de las Américas'
topics.problem: No problem signal.

topics.name: Targeting of social benefits
topics.problem: No signal found in this run (not verified as absent).

ideas: Sala Cuna fund financed by a 0.30% employer contribution offset by lower unemployment-insurance contributions
bills: Boletín 14.782-13, second stage; Cámara Hacienda committee next
T07.evidenceNote: Meta-analyses find more childcare raises maternal employment; Chilean primary studies on the Art. 203 mandate exist. Co-payment design: primary studies, no synthesis.

T08.evidenceNote: Meta-analyses on fiscal rules and deficits. Which cuts do the least harm: no synthesis found.

ideas: Raise primary-care per-capita funding without merging programmes
T09.evidenceNote: Reviews on primary-care strengthening and immunisation uptake. Cuts to high-cost coverage: no synthesis found.

entrepreneurs: Opposition members of the mixed committee
T14.evidenceNote: Hardware-only programmes show small learning effects; pedagogy-linked software does better. SLEP staffing: no evidence found.

ideas: Keep the place-based Calles sin Violencia model
T02.evidenceNote: Campbell reviews on hot-spots policing and focused deterrence show crime reductions. Neither plan has a published impact evaluation; one released before 30 Nov could discriminate between them.

ideas: Exclude sexual crimes against minors and crimes against humanity
T04.evidenceNote: No synthesis on administrative sentence-reduction regimes; reviews exist on sex-offender treatment and recidivism. No evidence-based alternative in this window.

T05.evidenceNote: Primary studies on default and life-cycle funds; no synthesis on derivative-risk limits; no evidence found on compensation. This window lacks a viable alternative.

T06.evidenceNote: Meta-analyses of active labour-market programmes. No hiring subsidy proposed.

ideas: Specific vape tax set below cigarette rates
T12.evidenceNote: IARC Handbook vol. 14: sufficient evidence that tobacco taxes prevent initiation and uptake among young people. Trigger: Hacienda filing the bill.

calendar.label: Hacienda committee and floor; target before Feb

context.executive: President José Antonio Kast (Partido Republicano), in office since 11 March 2026.
context.approvalNote: Cadem monthly averages: September 35%, October 30%. Approval fell below 30% in W7 and reached 26% on 1 Nov, the lowest since March.
problems: CEP 96 priorities: crime 57%, health 42%, education 28%, drug trafficking 28%, pensions 18%.
Cadem (1 Nov): worry about job instability 71% (+9).
Feedback Research (20–30 Oct): household economy (61%) overtakes neighbourhood crime (59%).
context.budget: Budget Law 2027 submitted 30 Sep (+1.5% spending). Mixed committee (29 Oct–5 Nov) rejected Education, primary care, SENCE and parts of Customs, Interior and Culture. Cámara floor 9–11 Nov, Senate 17–19 Nov, deadline 30 Nov (one source gives 29 Nov).
context.cabinet: Undersecretary of Justice removed 30 Oct; 59 senior departures since March. The President ruled out a cabinet change (5 Nov).

steps: Cross-cutting politics scan: approval polls, cabinet events, budget calendar and votes.
Re-checked the 10 topics from the October scan and added 10 more across ministries.
Official statistics: INE employment bulletin 336, Minsal waiting-list report, Fiscal Council reports.
Congress records through media reports of sessions and votes; Sala Cuna and vape-tax stages verified.
Coded 89 items; assigned stream levels per topic and week; detected windows; ran policy checks on 9 topics.
method.volume: 18 web searches, about 170 results screened, 89 items coded.
rules: A stream level carries forward up to 2 weeks without new items, then drops one level.
Executive signals take precedence over congressional ones.
A mixed-committee rejection of a budget chapter counts as blocking and lowers politics by one level.
limitations: Congress open data (senado.cl, camara.cl) and InfoLobby not queried directly; urgencies come from media.
Cadem September weekly values not retrieved; no Chilean poll aggregator identified.
Talk shows and podcasts not covered systematically (1 item).
Evidence repositories not queried; evidence states come from analyst knowledge and need verification.
Topics not verified (grey, not absent): constitutional security reform, ACOT bills, housing, water, environmental permitting, lithium, gender violence, state modernisation, social-benefit targeting.
Weekly levels are reliable from W4; W1–W3 are thin except for Sala Cuna. Weeks with no observation are shown as 'not observed'.
Single analyst, no double coding yet. Ratings are provisional.
validation: Sala Cuna (Senate vote 8 Sep): flagged in W1 as an open window on the decision agenda. Pass.
Rules on the Use of Force (7 Oct) and expulsions (20 Oct): flagged, then moved to closed/closing. Pass.
Sentence reductions: detected in W7, with up to 7 days of lag. Pass.

Risks: Colombia's vape tax would have produced a false positive without a country filter; pension losses became visible only when the regulator reported them; secondary outlets give conflicting poll figures.
nextVersion: Add a country filter to collection.
Make the mixed-committee blocking rule explicit.
Add the decay rule to the protocol.
Require senado.cl, camara.cl and InfoLobby data for confidence grade A.
